name: Amethyst
physical: Many people keep it nearby for relaxation during stressful times
summary: Amethyst is the purple quartz of calm and intuition, loved by crystal healers for restful sleep, meditation and spiritual protection. Meaning, care and lore.
intro: Amethyst is quartz colored violet by traces of iron and natural radiation, and it ranges from pale lilac to a deep, wine-dark purple. It forms in huge hollow geodes lined with sparkling points, and in slender clusters that glow in a sunny window. Prized for centuries, it was once as costly as ruby until enormous deposits turned up in Brazil. Today it is among the best-loved stones for beginners and collectors, partly for its beauty and partly for the gentle, soothing mood people say it brings. A fine piece shows even color with a faint reddish flash in good light.
history: The name comes from the Greek amethystos, meaning not intoxicated, because the Greeks believed the stone guarded its wearer against drunkenness. Wine goblets were carved from it, and a legend tells of the nymph Amethyst, turned to crystal by Artemis and stained with wine by Dionysus. Medieval bishops wore amethyst rings to signal piety, giving the stone its nickname. Egyptians set it in amulets, and European royalty favored it in crowns and scepters. Until Brazilian geodes were found in the 1800s, deep purple stones were rare and treasured.
meaning: Amethyst is the classic stone of peace of mind. Crystal healers associate it with the third eye and crown chakras, where it is said to quiet mental chatter and open the door to intuition. People turn to it for evening wind-downs, meditation and dream work, believing it helps the day's worries settle. Its old reputation for sobriety has grown into a wider symbolism of clear-headed choices, healthy boundaries and breaking unhelpful habits. Many see it as a protective stone for the aura, shielding the sensitive from overwhelming surroundings. In emotional work it is linked to comfort during grief and the patience needed through change. It is also considered a stone of spiritual devotion, which is why monks and meditators have long cherished it. Physical associations are gentle: restful sleep and ease through tension.
howToUse: Place a small cluster or tumbled stone on your nightstand or tuck it under your pillow to encourage restful sleep and vivid dream recall. Hold a palm stone against your brow during meditation to focus on the third eye. A geode in the corner of a bedroom is a favorite feng shui touch for a calm retreat. Wear amethyst pendants or rings as a daily reminder to pause before reacting. Set a point in your workspace to soften a busy atmosphere, or add it to a grid for peace and protection. Keep a piece in your bag during stressful travel days.
care: Amethyst fades with prolonged strong sunlight, so never leave it on a sunny sill; moonlight is the better charging choice. It is hard enough for a quick rinse in cool water, then dry it gently. Smoke from sage or palo santo, a bowl of brown rice, or a selenite plate all cleanse it well. Avoid heat, which can turn amethyst yellow or pale. Store it away from harder stones such as topaz or sapphire, and wrap points so the tips stay unchipped.
identify: Genuine amethyst often shows uneven color zoning, with paler tips and deeper bases or angular color bands. Glass imitations are perfectly uniform and may contain round bubbles. Dyed purple agate or quartz can look flat and may leave color in cracks. Lab-grown amethyst exists and is hard to spot without testing. Heated amethyst becomes citrine, and stone sold as lavender quartz may be mixed. Natural geodes are heavy with matte brown exteriors; hollow sparkly shells with painted finishes are suspect.

faq.a: Amethyst is traditionally used for calm, intuition and sleep. Crystal healers link it to the third eye and crown chakras, and many people keep it nearby for peaceful evenings, meditation and a protective, steady feeling during stressful periods.

faq.q: Can amethyst go in the sun?
faq.a: It is best not to. Prolonged strong sunlight can fade amethyst, and heat may change its color entirely. Charge it under moonlight, or on a selenite plate, and display it away from bright direct windows.

faq.q: Which side of the house should amethyst go on?
faq.a: Many feng shui practitioners place amethyst in a bedroom, meditation corner or the knowledge area of the home. There is no strict rule, and the best spot is wherever you will see it and feel calmer.
